_comment: Purchasable product records, keyed by catalogue slug (slugify of the agent name on /agents). name and sku are what Stripe, the success page and invoices show. A slug with no record here, or with saleApproved=false, blocks LIVE-mode checkout (default-deny); only saleApproved=true opens live sales. Test-mode keys are unaffected, so enabling a test checkout can never start real sales of an unapproved release. release.package is the object name under agents/<slug>/ in private storage (Vercel Private Blob, or R2) that a buyer downloads; release.sha256 must equal the hash of that exact uploaded file (null = not yet published, the success page then omits it). aliases: retired slugs that must keep resolving to this product (old checkout links, Stripe metadata, KV entitlements and certificates written before a rename). Version-specific entitlements (lib/releaseAccess.js): each purchase records the release version it bought, and a buyer may download that release, and a later release only as far as Continuous Certification covers it. When a new release replaces "release", move the old record (with its package and sha256) into "previousReleases" so its buyers keep it, and give every new release a "releasedAt" ISO date (certification coverage after a lapse is judged by it). A corrective release (a defect fix for releases already sold) lists them in "correctiveFor" (e.g. ["1.0.3.2"]) and goes to their buyers without certification. legacyEntitlementVersion: the release a purchase recorded before version pinning counts as.
